practiceReport.name: Jordan Addison
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (92% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Addison is in recovery mode from the thumb injury that required surgery following a Nov. 15 practice, and he's missed the last two games as a result. While an IR stint has been ruled out for Addison, O'Connell relayed Monday that the wide receiver is "progressing really well" but also isn't expected to play Sunday against the Falcons, according to Goessling. As long as Addison is sidelined, some combination of Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price will operate alongside top WR Justin Jefferson.

practiceReport.name: Isaiah Rodgers
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (83% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Rodgers was unable to play against the 49ers in Week 11 due to a quadriceps injury. He hasn't been cleared to practice since picking up the injury during last Thursday's session, and he'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.

practiceReport.name: Harrison Smith
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Smith may have injured his thigh during the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Week 11, when he logged two tackles (one solo). He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation, and a full session would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.

practiceReport.name: Kyler Murray
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Dual-threat QB; rushing workload can be scaled when managing lower-extremity tags.
factors: Returned to Limited Participation (LP) on Wednesday following 3-game absence
practiceReport.beatComment: Murray hasn't been available for any of the Vikings' last three games while recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring strain, but his ability to kick off Week 12 prep with a limited showing bodes well for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Falcons. The 29-year-old signal-caller has started in each of his prior six appearances this season but will be in line for a backup role once healthy after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins on Nov. 10 and immediately installed him as their new starter.

practiceReport.name: Tai Felton
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
practiceReport.beatComment: Felton has had increased sway in the Vikings offense the past two games with Jordan Addison sidelined, combining for nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards. Addison is trending toward another absence Sunday against the Falcons, so Felton is in line to continue his elevated role this weekend, assuming he's able to play through his hip injury.

practiceReport.name: Myles Price
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
practiceReport.beatComment: The knee issue is a new concern for Price, who was anything other than a full participant in practice for the first time all season as the Vikings kicked off Week 12 prep. If Price is able to advance to full activity by Friday, he should be in good position to head into Sunday's game against the Falcons without an injury designation. Price typically sees most of his snaps on special teams when the Vikings receiver room is at full strength, but he's seen his playing time on offense pick up over the past three weeks while Jordan Addison has been sidelined with a thumb injury.

practiceReport.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (8th NFL season, 79% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

practiceReport.name: T.J. Hockenson
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Hockenson showed promising chemistry with Kirk Cousins after the veteran TE sat out Cousins' return to Minnesota during the Week 10 win over Green Bay. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

practiceReport.name: Jeshaun Jones
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Demond Claiborne
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Bo Richter
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Donovan Jackson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 6 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dwight McGlothern Jr.
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: 4-game minimum satisfied on Injured Reserve (Undisclosed); awaiting 21-day practice window designation.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Josh Oliver
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 6 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Samac
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 6 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Samac appeared on the Vikings' injury report during Week 3 prep with a new knee injury. The backup center's issue must be significant, as he was promptly moved to IR. Samac will need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the Vikings' active roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jamal Adams
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026

irAndReserveTracker.name: Tyler Batty
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Batty suffered a torn ACL during Friday's preseason loss to the Broncos and will now be forced to miss the upcoming season. He logged 12 tackles (nine solo) across 12 games with Minnesota last season and will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.
